claim: Second primary cancers (SPCs) are a rare but severe complication of curative-intent radiation therapy.
source: A rare but severe complication of curative-intent radiation therapy is the induction of second primary cancers.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and introduction, supported by citations to literature on SPCs.

claim: SPCs preferentially develop not inside the planning target volume (PTV) but around it, over several centimeters.
source: These cancers preferentially develop not inside the planning target volume (PTV) but around, over several centimeters, after a latency period of 1–40 years.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Diallo et al., 2009; Dörr and Herrmann, 2002).

claim: SPCs have a latency period of 1–40 years after radiation therapy.
source: These cancers preferentially develop not inside the planning target volume (PTV) but around, over several centimeters, after a latency period of 1–40 years.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Berrington de Gonzalez et al., 2013; Dörr and Herrmann, 2002; Doyen et al., 2010; Sheppard and Libshitz, 2001; Tubiana, 2009; Vautravers et al., 2010).

claim: Normal human or mouse dermal fibroblasts submitted to the out-of-field dose at the margin of a PTV do not die but enter a long-lived senescent state.
source: We show here that normal human or mouse dermal fibroblasts submitted to the out-of-field dose scattering at the margin of a PTV receiving a mimicked patient's treatment do not die but enter in a long-lived senescent state resulting from the accumulation of unrepaired DNA single-strand breaks, in the almost absence of double-strand breaks.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: The senescent state of fibroblasts at the margin results from the accumulation of unrepaired DNA single-strand breaks, in the almost absence of double-strand breaks.
source: We show here that normal human or mouse dermal fibroblasts submitted to the out-of-field dose scattering at the margin of a PTV receiving a mimicked patient's treatment do not die but enter in a long-lived senescent state resulting from the accumulation of unrepaired DNA single-strand breaks, in the almost absence of double-strand breaks.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: A few senescent cells at the margin systematically and spontaneously escape from cell cycle arrest to generate daughter cells harboring mutations and invasive capacities.
source: Importantly, a few of these senescent cells systematically and spontaneously escape from the cell cycle arrest after a while to generate daughter cells harboring mutations and invasive capacities.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: Single-strand break-induced senescence is the mechanism of second primary cancer initiation.
source: These findings highlight single-strand break-induced senescence as the mechanism of second primary cancer initiation, with clinically relevant spatiotemporal specificities.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the study.

claim: The increased risk of developing an SPC after radiation therapy ranges from 0 to 14 in available studies.
source: Data on the increased risk of developing an SPC after radiation therapy is quite divergent in the available studies: it ranges from 0 in a cohort of 13,457 patients with rectal cancer having received radiation therapy after surgery compared to surgery alone (Martling et al., 2017) to 14 in a cohort of 1136 patients diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma at a median age of 11 years (Holmqvist et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to specific studies.

claim: SPCs are highly suspected to be radiation-induced, although the causal relationship is impossible to definitely prove.
source: Although the causal relationship between the initial radiation therapy and the induction of the SPC is impossible to definitely prove, SPCs are highly suspected to be radiation-induced.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and reflects the current understanding in the field.

claim: Lifestyle, exogenous stressors, and genetic factors could be contributing factors to SPC development.
source: However, lifestyle, exogenous stressors, and genetic factors could also be contributing factors (Doyen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The marginal dose in radiation therapy has three characteristics: (i) the deposited dose exponentially decreases with distance, (ii) the deposited dose is approximately proportional to the PTV size, and (iii) the photon's spectral energy fluence distribution is shifted to lower energies compared with those inside the PTV.
source: The marginal radiation has three characteristics: (i) the deposited dose exponentially decreases with the distance, (ii) the deposited dose is approximately proportional to the PTV size, and (iii) the photon's spectral energy fluence distribution is shifted to lower energies compared with those inside the PTV (Chofor et al., 2012; Chofor et al., 2011; Kirkby et al., 2007; Kry et al., 2007; Wiezorek et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The photon quality change at the margin has the potential to increase the relative biological effectiveness (RBE).
source: It was suggested that this photon quality change has the potential to increase the relative biological effectiveness (RBE) (Chofor et al., 2011; Kirkby et al., 2007), but the underlying specific cellular damages, if any, are unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations, but noted as speculative.

claim: X-rays induce DNA single-strand breaks (SSBs) and double-strand breaks (DSBs).
source: X-rays induce, among others, DNA single-strand breaks (SSBs) and double-strand breaks (DSBs) (Azzam et al., 2012; Jonathan et al., 1999; Panganiban et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: DSBs are defined as two breaks in the sugar-phosphate backbone on each DNA strand, at less than 10 bp.
source: DSBs are defined as two breaks in the sugar-phosphate backbone on each DNA strand, at less than 10 bp.
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction.

claim: An SSB is a break in the sugar-phosphate backbone on only one DNA strand, often accompanied by a nucleotide loss and often displaying abnormal 5′ and 3′ ends.
source: An SSB is a break in the sugar-phosphate backbone on only one DNA strand, often accompanied by a nucleotide loss and often displaying abnormal 5′ and 3′ ends (Caldecott, 2008).
evidence: This is a definition provided in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The SSB repair (SSBR) pathway involves a first step of break detection initiated by the poly(ADP)ribose polymerase (PARP) 1.
source: The SSB repair (SSBR) pathway involves a first step of break detection initiated by the poly(ADP)ribose polymerase (PARP) 1, which, once activated by its linkage to the broken DNA, synthetizes long chains of poly(ADP)ribose (PAR).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and reflects established knowledge about SSBR.

claim: The curative effect of ionizing radiations results from the formation of DSBs too many to be repaired, leading to cancer cell death by apoptosis or mitotic catastrophe.
source: It is known for a long time that the curative effect of ionizing radiations results from the formation of DSBs too many to be repaired, leading to cancer cell death by apoptosis or mitotic catastrophe (Jonathan et al., 1999; Norbury and Hickson, 2001; Panganiban et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: 1 Gy deposited in the PTV generates 10–25 more SSBs than DSBs.
source: SSBs are less detrimental than DSBs, but 1 Gy deposited in the PTV generates 10–25 more SSBs than DSBs (Dahm-Daphi et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Nothing is known about the respective quantities of SSBs and DSBs generated in the margin of the PTV and the consequences on the outcome of the affected normal cells.
source: Presently, nothing is known about the respective quantities of SSBs and DSBs generated in the margin of the PTV and the consequences on the outcome of the affected normal cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a knowledge gap that the study addresses.

claim: The cumulative incidence of SPCs increases with time.
source: Moreover, the cumulative incidence of SPCs increases with time (Doyen et al., 2010; Friedman et al., 2010; Olsen et al., 2009; Storm, 1988): for instance, the cumulative incidence of second sarcoma in a cohort of 16,705 patients treated by radiation therapy for nonmetastatic breast carcinoma was calculated at 0.7% at 5 years, at 0.27% at 10 years, and at 0.48% at 15 years after the initial treatment time (Kirova et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Senescence is a reprogrammed state established to adapt to several stresses, such as telomere shortening, DNA damages, oxidative damages, or hyperactivation of some oncogenes.
source: Indeed, although initially described as the state reached by normal human fibroblasts after a finite doubling number, senescence is now recognized as a more general reprogrammed state established to adapt to several stresses, such as telomere shortening, DNA damages, oxidative damages, or hyperactivation of some oncogenes (Abbadie et al., 2017; Ben-Porath and Weinberg, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Ionizing radiations are senescence inducers.
source: By producing DNA damages and oxidative stress, ionizing radiations are senescence inducers (Cmielová et al., 2011; Panganiban et al., 2013; Seol et al., 2012; Suzuki et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The senescence program includes an increase in cell size, complex epigenetic changes, an increase in reticulum endoplasmic stress, an increase in autophagy, changes in the composition of the secretome, and a long-term cell cycle arrest in G1 associated with a resistance to apoptosis.
source: The senescence program includes an increase in cell size, complex epigenetic changes, an increase in reticulum endoplasmic stress, an increase in autophagy, changes in the composition of the secretome, and above all a long-term cell cycle arrest in G1 associated with a resistance to apoptosis, making senescent cells nonproliferating long-lived cells in vivo (Abbadie et al., 2017; Martien and Abbadie, 2007; Pluquet et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: When unrepaired DNA damages are signalized through the DDR pathway, such as DSBs or shortened telomeres, the cell cycle arrest is very stable, almost irreversible, and considered as tumor suppressor.
source: When these damages are of a type signalized through the DDR pathway, such as DSBs or shortened telomeres, the cell cycle arrest is very stable, almost irreversible, considered as tumor suppressor (Campisi and d'Adda di Fagagna, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: When the unrepaired damages are SSBs, about one senescent cell on 10,000 systematically and spontaneously re-enters in cell cycle to give rise to a progeny of cells named post-senescent neoplastic emergent (PSNE) cells.
source: In contrast, when the unrepaired damages are SSBs, as we have shown in a seminal work on endogenous oxidative stress-induced senescence, about one senescent cell on 10,000 systematically and spontaneously re-enters in cell cycle to give rise to a progeny of cells we named post-senescent neoplastic emergent (PSNE) cells.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and refers to previous work by the authors.

claim: PSNE cells display mutations, markers of transformation, markers of epithelial-to-mesenchyme transition, and are able to form small hyperplasias or carcinomas in in vivo assays.
source: These cells display mutations, markers of transformation, markers of epithelial-to-mesenchyme transition, and are able to form small hyperplasias or carcinomas in in vivo assays (Deruy et al., 2010; Gosselin et al., 2009a; Malaquin et al., 2013; Martin et al., 2014; Nassour et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The maximum dose was deposited at 16–30 mm deep for 6 MV and at 25–45 mm deep for 20 MV.
source: The results indicated that the maximum dose was deposited at 16–30 mm deep for 6 MV and at 25–45 mm deep for 20 MV (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a result from characterizing the depth profile of the linear accelerator, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MDA-MB231 cells positioned inside the PTV underwent cell death after 3 weeks of irradiation.
source: As expected, both MDA-MB231 and NHDFs positioned inside the PTV underwent cell death after 3 weeks of irradiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A.

claim: NHDFs positioned inside the PTV underwent cell death after 3 weeks of irradiation.
source: As expected, both MDA-MB231 and NHDFs positioned inside the PTV underwent cell death after 3 weeks of irradiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: NHDFs positioned in the margin did not die.
source: In contrast, NHDFs positioned in the margin did not die: those in the most distal margin continued to grow as control nonirradiated cells or underwent a slight slowdown, whereas those positioned in the most proximal margin underwent a growth arrest (Figure 1A and B, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: NHDFs positioned in the most distal margin continued to grow as control nonirradiated cells or underwent a slight slowdown.
source: In contrast, NHDFs positioned in the margin did not die: those in the most distal margin continued to grow as control nonirradiated cells or underwent a slight slowdown, whereas those positioned in the most proximal margin underwent a growth arrest (Figure 1A and B, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: NHDFs positioned in the most proximal margin underwent a growth arrest.
source: In contrast, NHDFs positioned in the margin did not die: those in the most distal margin continued to grow as control nonirradiated cells or underwent a slight slowdown, whereas those positioned in the most proximal margin underwent a growth arrest (Figure 1A and B, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: MDA-MB231 began to suffer from caspase-independent cell death after four radiation fractions.
source: The results indicated that MDA-MB231 began to suffer from caspase-independent cell death after four radiation fractions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: NHDFs positioned inside the PTV underwent cell death, but to a lower extent than MDA-MB231, both by caspase-dependent and -independent mechanisms.
source: In the meantime, NHDFs positioned inside the PTV also underwent cell death, but to a lower extent, both by caspase-dependent and -independent mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: NHDFs positioned at the margin, even the most proximal one, did not die at a significant level.
source: In contrast, NHDFs positioned at the margin, even the most proximal one, did not die at a significant level (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The SA-β-Gal activity increased with successive radiation fractions in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV or at the margin, up to 7 cm.
source: The results indicate that the SA-β-Gal activity increased with successive radiation fractions, both in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV or at the margin, up to 7 cm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2A and B.

claim: The SA-β-Gal activity reached in cells positioned inside the PTV aimed at that of replicative senescent NHDFs, whereas that reached in cells located at the margin was lower.
source: The activity reached in cells positioned inside the PTV aimed at that of replicative senescent NHDFs, whereas that reached in cells located at the margin was lower (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: Cell size and granularity increased with successive radiation fractions at significant levels in cells positioned at the margin.
source: Cell size and granularity also increased with successive radiation fractions at significant levels in cells positioned at the margin.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: In the PTV, cell size and granularity increased during the first week of treatment and then decreased.
source: In the PTV, cell size and granularity increased during the first week of treatment and then decreased (Figure 2A and C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: Two subpopulations appeared in the PTV after 3 weeks of irradiation: one comprising the biggest and most granular cells with a high SA-β-Gal activity (senescent cells), and another one comprising very granular but very small cells with a very low β-Gal activity (probably dying cells).
source: A careful examination of the dot plots and histograms indicated that two subpopulations appeared in the PTV after 3 weeks of irradiation: one comprising the biggest and most granular cells with a high SA-β-Gal activity, which are bona fide senescent cells, and another one comprising very granular but very small cells with a very low β-Gal activity, which probably correspond to dying cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: After 13 radiation fractions, NHDFs positioned at the margin were cell cycle arrested in G1, with even less cells in S phase than in a population of NHDFs at the replicative senescence plateau.
source: After 13 radiation fractions, NHDFs positioned at the margin were cell cycle arrested in G1, with even less cells in S phase than in a population of NHDFs at the replicative senescence plateau (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: For NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, p16 mRNA levels increased as soon as the second radiation fraction, but then dropped back during further radiation fractions.
source: For NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, the results show that p16 mRNA levels increased as soon as the second radiation fraction, but then dropped back during further radiation fractions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: For NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, p21 appeared to take the reins with an upregulation from the second week of irradiation.
source: p21 appeared to take the reins with an upregulation from the second week of irradiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: For NHDFs positioned in the margin, p16 and p21 mRNA levels followed approximately the same induction pattern, mainly from the end of the first week of irradiation.
source: For NHDFs positioned in the margin, p16 and p21 mRNA levels followed approximately the same induction pattern, mainly from the end of the first week of irradiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The level of p16 protein examined by Western blot and immunofluorescence followed the same expression pattern than the mRNA.
source: The level of p16 protein examined by Western blot and immunofluorescence followed the same expression pattern than the mRNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: The percentage of multinucleated cells approximately doubled in NHDFs positioned at the margin after 2 weeks of irradiation.
source: The results indicate that the percentage of multinucleated cells approximately doubled in NHDFs positioned at the margin after 2 weeks of irradiation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: The percentage of multinucleated cells did not significantly increase in NHDFs positioned in the PTV.
source: This percentage did not significantly increase in NHDFs positioned in the PTV (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 5.

claim: During a simulated radiation therapy protocol, NHDFs positioned at the margin of the PTV undergo senescence, whereas those positioned inside the PTV go through a senescent-like phenotype and then die.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that during a simulated radiation therapy protocol, NHDFs positioned at the margin of the PTV undergo senescence, whereas those positioned inside the PTV go through a senescent-like phenotype and then die.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the data presented in Figure 2 and supplements.

claim: In NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, both XRCC1 and 53BP1/γH2AX foci were detected.
source: In NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, we detected both XRCC1 and 53BP1/γH2AX foci as expected.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: In NHDFs positioned at the margin, almost only XRCC1 foci were detected.
source: In NHDFs positioned at the margin, we detected almost only XRCC1 foci.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: XRCC1 foci were as numerous in the margin as in the PTV, whatever the distance, up to 5 cm.
source: Surprisingly, they were as much numerous in the margin as in the PTV, whatever the distance, up to 5 cm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: The quantity of 53BP1/γH2AX foci per cell rapidly dropped down with the distance from the limit of the PTV.
source: In contrast, the quantity of 53BP1/γH2AX foci per cell rapidly dropped down with the distance from the limit of the PTV, as expected (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: Comet assay results at pH 12.3 revealed the presence of breaks in NHDFs positioned at the margin up to about 5 cm.
source: Comet assay results at pH 12.3 revealed the presence of breaks in NHDFs positioned at the margin up to about 5 cm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: Comet assay results at pH 8 confirmed the lack of DSB formation in NHDFs positioned at the margin.
source: Comet assay results at pH 8 confirmed the lack of DSB formation in NHDFs positioned at the margin (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: The breaks recorded in the margin correspond almost only to SSBs.
source: Therefore, the breaks recorded in the margin correspond almost only to SSBs, hence confirming the immunofluorescence results.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on comet assay data.

claim: SSBs were as numerous in the proximal and distal margins.
source: As in immunofluorescence results, SSBs were as numerous in the proximal and distal margins.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: Comet assay results confirmed the formation of both SSBs and DSBs in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV.
source: Comet assay results also confirmed the formation of both SSBs and DSBs in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3B.

claim: There was no statistically significant difference in the quantity of SSBs and DSBs generated inside the PTV or at the margin after one irradiation at 2 Gy at 6 or 20 MV.
source: The results indicate that there was no statistically significant difference in the quantity of SSBs and DSBs generated inside the PTV or at the margin after one irradiation at 2 Gy at 6 or 20 MV (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: A unitary 2 Gy irradiation generates in nontumoral fibroblasts surrounding the PTV a specific SSB-without-DSB signature.
source: Therefore, a unitary 2 Gy irradiation generates in nontumoral fibroblasts surrounding the PTV a specific SSB-without-DSB signature.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the data presented.

claim: The quantity of the generated DSBs followed approximately the dose gradient that exponentially decreases from the PTV to the most distal margin.
source: As expected (Hagen, 1994), the quantity of the generated DSBs followed approximately the dose gradient that exponentially decreases from the PTV to the most distal margin.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: The quantity of generated SSBs was almost constant from the PTV to the most distal margin assayed (about 5 cm).
source: In contrast and surprisingly, the quantity of generated SSBs was almost constant from the PTV to the most distal margin assayed here (about 5 cm).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: XRCC1 foci were recorded in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV and at the margin in only the first plate when the two plates were not sealed, but also in the second plate, when the plates were sealed, up to 18.7 cm.
source: Regarding SSBs, we recorded XRCC1 foci in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV and at the margin in only the first plate when the two plates were not sealed, but also in the second plate, when the plates were sealed, up to 18.7 cm.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 5B.

claim: 53BP1 foci were recorded only in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV and, to a much less extent, in the most proximal margin of the first plate.
source: Regarding DSBs, we recorded 53BP1 foci only in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV and, to a much less extent, in the most proximal margin of the first plate, confirming the previous results (Figure 3—figure supplement 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 5B.

claim: SSBs are generated by ionizing particles that propagate inside the material.
source: This result suggests that SSBs are generated by ionizing particles that propagate inside the material, here in the plastic of the culture plates.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the experiment with sealed plates.

claim: There was no difference in SSB plus DSB quantity generated in cells positioned in the margin when cultured in 0.1% FBS compared to 2%.
source: The results indicate that there was no difference in SSB plus DSB quantity generated in cells positioned in the margin when cultured in 0.1% FBS compared to 2% (Figure 3—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 6.

claim: Both SSBs and DSBs developed in dermal cells of total body-irradiated mice.
source: As expected, both SSBs and DSBs developed in dermal cells of total body-irradiated mice.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: Only SSBs, but not DSBs, were generated in dermal cells of the skin of mice positioned at the margin of the phantom, up to 2 cm from the contact with the phantom.
source: In contrast, only SSBs, but not DSBs, were generated in dermal cells of the skin of mice positioned at the margin of the phantom, up to 2 cm from the contact with the phantom (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: Most of the XRCC1-positive dermal cells were fibroblasts.
source: By co-detecting vimentin with XRCC1, we showed that most of the XRCC1-positive dermal cells were fibroblasts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The peri-PTV in vivo tissues also specifically develop an SSB-without-DSB signature upon irradiation.
source: Therefore, the peri-PTV in vivo tissues also specifically develop an SSB-without-DSB signature upon irradiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the mouse experiment data.

claim: Regarding DSBs in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, there was no significant difference between cells irradiated once or five times.
source: Regarding DSBs in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, the results of comet assays at pH 8 show that there was no significant difference between cells irradiated once or five times.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Regarding DSBs in NHDFs positioned at the margin, the results confirmed their almost absence.
source: Regarding DSBs in NHDFs positioned at the margin, the results confirmed again their almost absence.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: In NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, SSBs were less numerous after five irradiations than after just one.
source: Regarding SSBs, the comparison of the results at pH 8 and 12.3 indicated that in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV, SSBs were less numerous after five irradiations than after just one.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: In NHDFs positioned at the margin, SSBs were more numerous after five irradiations than after just one.
source: In contrast, in NHDFs positioned at the margin, SSBs were more numerous after five irradiations than after just one (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: The SSBs generated in NHDFs positioned at the margin accumulate with successive radiation fractions.
source: Therefore, the SSBs generated in NHDFs positioned at the margin accumulate with successive radiation fractions, in contrast to both DSBs and SSBs generated in cells positioned inside the PTV that do not.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the comet assay data.

claim: DSBs and SSBs generated in cells positioned inside the PTV do not accumulate with successive radiation fractions.
source: Therefore, the SSBs generated in NHDFs positioned at the margin accumulate with successive radiation fractions, in contrast to both DSBs and SSBs generated in cells positioned inside the PTV that do not.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the comet assay data.

claim: SSBs formed in cells positioned either in the PTV or the margin were fully repaired within 72 hr after a unique irradiation.
source: The results indicate that SSBs formed in cells positioned either in the PTV or the margin were fully repaired within 72 hr after a unique irradiation, whereas they were still detected 72 hr after the last irradiation of a series of five (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that the SSB repair capacity decreased with successive radiation fractions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: SSBs were still detected 72 hr after the last irradiation of a series of five.
source: The results indicate that SSBs formed in cells positioned either in the PTV or the margin were fully repaired within 72 hr after a unique irradiation, whereas they were still detected 72 hr after the last irradiation of a series of five (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that the SSB repair capacity decreased with successive radiation fractions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The SSB repair capacity decreased with successive radiation fractions.
source: The results indicate that SSBs formed in cells positioned either in the PTV or the margin were fully repaired within 72 hr after a unique irradiation, whereas they were still detected 72 hr after the last irradiation of a series of five (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that the SSB repair capacity decreased with successive radiation fractions.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the comet assay data.

claim: The DSBs were always fully repaired within 72 hr, whatever the cells were submitted to one or five radiation fractions.
source: In contrast, the DSBs were always fully repaired within 72 hr, whatever the cells were submitted to one or five radiation fractions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that the DSB repair capacity was not affected along a fractionated irradiation protocol.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The DSB repair capacity was not affected along a fractionated irradiation protocol.
source: In contrast, the DSBs were always fully repaired within 72 hr, whatever the cells were submitted to one or five radiation fractions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), indicating that the DSB repair capacity was not affected along a fractionated irradiation protocol.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the comet assay data.

claim: XRCC1 foci (SSBs) generated in the PTV were partly resolved within 72 hr.
source: The same results were obtained by analyzing the breaks by immunofluorescence against XRCC1 and 53BP1: XRCC1 foci (SSBs) generated in the PTV were also partly resolved within 72 hr, but those generated in the margin were still significantly present after 72 hr; 53BP1 foci (DSBs) present in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV or at the proximal margin after four successive radiation fractions at 2 Gy were partly resolved within 72 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: XRCC1 foci (SSBs) generated in the margin were still significantly present after 72 hr.
source: The same results were obtained by analyzing the breaks by immunofluorescence against XRCC1 and 53BP1: XRCC1 foci (SSBs) generated in the PTV were also partly resolved within 72 hr, but those generated in the margin were still significantly present after 72 hr; 53BP1 foci (DSBs) present in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV or at the proximal margin after four successive radiation fractions at 2 Gy were partly resolved within 72 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: 53BP1 foci (DSBs) present in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV or at the proximal margin after four successive radiation fractions at 2 Gy were partly resolved within 72 hr.
source: The same results were obtained by analyzing the breaks by immunofluorescence against XRCC1 and 53BP1: XRCC1 foci (SSBs) generated in the PTV were also partly resolved within 72 hr, but those generated in the margin were still significantly present after 72 hr; 53BP1 foci (DSBs) present in NHDFs positioned inside the PTV or at the proximal margin after four successive radiation fractions at 2 Gy were partly resolved within 72 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: After one irradiation NHDFs do synthesize PAR chains in response to H2O2, whereas after 10 successive radiation fractions they have become unable to do so.
source: Immunofluorescence against PAR chains shows that after one irradiation NHDFs do synthesize PAR chains in response to H2O2, whereas after 10 successive radiation fractions they have become unable to do so (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: The successive irradiations of a standard fractioned radiotherapy protocol could lead to an exhaustion of the PARylation capacity, provoking the accumulation of unrepaired SSBs.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the successive irradiations of a standard fractioned radiotherapy protocol could lead to an exhaustion of the PARylation capacity, provoking the accumulation of unrepaired SSBs.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the data presented.

claim: After 2–4 weeks post-sorting, small proliferating cells appeared amongst senescent cells emanating from the margin, referred to as post-senescent neoplastic emergent (PSNE).
source: After 2–4 weeks post-sorting according to the experiment, we noticed the reappearance of small proliferating cells amongst senescent cells emanating from the margin (Figure 6A and B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A) referred to as post-senescent neoplastic emergent (PSNE).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6A and B.

claim: PSNE cells, having emerged from senescent cells of the margin, resisted the 6-TG treatment, suggesting they were carrying mutations.
source: In contrast, PSNE cells, having emerged from senescent cells of the margin, resisted the 6-TG treatment, suggesting they were carrying mutations (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6C.

claim: Gelatinase activity was detected in PSNE cells emanating from NHDFs positioned in the margin compared to exponentially growing NHDFs taken as control.
source: Gelatinase activity was detected in PSNE cells emanating from NHDFs positioned in the margin compared to exponentially growing NHDFs taken as control (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6D.

claim: PSNE cells, having emerged from senescence induced in the margin, did not show any increased migration compared to nonirradiated exponentially growing cells.
source: PSNE cells, having emerged from senescence induced in the margin, did not show any increased migration compared to nonirradiated exponentially growing cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6E.

claim: The invasive capacities of PSNE cells were multiplied about fourfold compared to control cells.
source: However, their invasive capacities were multiplied about fourfold compared to control cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6E.

claim: Up to 10 months after grafting, none of the mice grafted with 10^6 PSNE cells emanating from NHDFs positioned in the margin developed tumors.
source: Up to now, 10 months after grafting, none of these mice developed tumors, whereas all mice grafted with HT1080 cells, a sarcoma cell line, developed a tumor within 2 weeks.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and represents experimental data from xenograft experiments.

claim: All mice grafted with HT1080 cells, a sarcoma cell line, developed a tumor within 2 weeks.
source: Up to now, 10 months after grafting, none of these mice developed tumors, whereas all mice grafted with HT1080 cells, a sarcoma cell line, developed a tumor within 2 weeks.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and represents experimental data from xenograft experiments.

claim: Along irradiations of a fractionated protocol normal fibroblasts of the vicinity of a PTV enter premature senescence from which, after a while, few rare cells evade to give rise to a progeny of proliferative, mutated, invading, but not fully tumorigenic cells.
source: Taken together, these results evidence that along irradiations of a fractionated protocol normal fibroblasts of the vicinity of a PTV enter premature senescence from which, after a while, few rare cells evade to give rise to a progeny of proliferative, mutated, invading, but not fully tumorigenic cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the data presented in Figure 6.

claim: The combined treatment of H2O2 and veliparib induced a significant accumulation of XRCC1 foci, beginning from the 14th day of the combined treatment.
source: We checked that the combined treatment did induce a significant accumulation of XRCC1 foci, whereas the treatments with H2O2 alone or veliparib alone were very much less efficient. The accumulation of XRCC1 foci began from the 14th day of the combined treatment (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7A.

claim: The combined treatment of H2O2 and veliparib did not induce an accumulation of DSBs, oxidative base damages visualized by OGG1 foci, or oxidative damage to mitochondria analyzed with the JC1 probe.
source: We also checked that the combined treatment did not induce either an accumulation of DSBs, oxidative base damages visualized by OGG1 foci, or oxidative damage to mitochondria analyzed with the JC1 probe (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The accumulation of unrepaired SSBs resulted in a rise in the number of SA-β-Gal-positive cells.
source: We observed a rise in the number of SA-β-Gal-positive cells (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 3A, B, Figure 7—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7B.

claim: The SA-β-Gal activity rising was correlated with a cell growth arrest from the 25th day.
source: This SA-β-Gal activity rising was correlated with a cell growth arrest from the 25th day (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 3A), an increased cell size, spreading and granularity (Figure 7D, Figure 7—figure supplement 4A), an upregulation of p16 expression, and a hypophosphorylation of Rb (Figure 7—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7C.

claim: A specific accumulation of SSBs only results in premature senescence.
source: These data attest that a specific accumulation of SSBs only results in premature senescence.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the H2O2 + veliparib treatment data.

claim: A growth recovery was observed from the days 35–50 due to the appearance in the culture dishes of small cells with a stellate shape.
source: We observed a growth recovery from the days 35–50 according to the experiment (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 3A) due to the appearance in the culture dishes of small cells with a stellate shape (Figure 7D), which were SA-β-Gal negative (Figure 7B) and resistant to 6-TG in HPRT assays (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7C and D.

claim: The small cells that appeared after senescence were SA-β-Gal negative and resistant to 6-TG in HPRT assays.
source: We observed a growth recovery from the days 35–50 according to the experiment (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 3A) due to the appearance in the culture dishes of small cells with a stellate shape (Figure 7D), which were SA-β-Gal negative (Figure 7B) and resistant to 6-TG in HPRT assays (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 7B and E.

claim: The sole SSB accumulation in the absence of DSBs or other damages is sufficient to induce a premature senescent state from which a few cells escape to generate reproliferating, morphologically transformed and mutated daughter cells.
source: All these results suggest that the sole SSB accumulation in the absence of DSBs or other damages is sufficient to induce a premature senescent state from which a few cells escape to generate reproliferating, morphologically transformed and mutated daughter cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the H2O2 + veliparib treatment data.

claim: The out-of-field dose induces the formation of SSBs, but nearly no DSBs.
source: We show that the out-of-field dose induces the formation of SSBs, but nearly no DSBs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The SSBs accumulate during a mimicked standard therapeutic protocol because of a lack of repair due to a decrease in the PARylation capacity that establishes along the successive daily radiation fractions.
source: Importantly, the SSBs accumulate during a mimicked standard therapeutic protocol because of a lack of repair due to a decrease in the PARylation capacity that establishes along the successive daily radiation fractions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: The fibroblasts affected by the specific accumulation of unrepaired SSBs do not undergo cell death but enter in premature senescence.
source: The fibroblasts affected by this specific accumulation of unrepaired SSBs do not undergo cell death but enter in premature senescence.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: A few senescent cells re-enter cell cycle to generate a progeny of daughter cells displaying hallmarks of cancerous transformation, but which have not become fully tumorigenic.
source: They remain stably arrested in this senescent state for a while, and then a few of them re-enter cell cycle to generate a progeny of daughter cells displaying hallmarks of cancerous transformation, but which have not become fully tumorigenic.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: This scenario is the first that could explain at the same time the latency period of second sarcoma emergence and the preferential location of second sarcomas around the treated volume.
source: It is, to our knowledge, the first scenario that could explain at the same time the latency period of second sarcoma emergence, underpinned by the long life of senescent cells, and the preferential location of second sarcomas around the treated volume, underpinned by the specific accumulation in this area of nonlethal but mutagenic unrepaired DNA damages.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion drawn from the findings.

claim: The quantity of DSBs dramatically decreases from a few millimeters from the limit of the beam.
source: In accordance, we found that the quantity of DSBs dramatically decreases from a few millimeters from the limit of the beam.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by the experimental data.

claim: SSBs were almost as numerous at several centimeters from the limit of the beam as inside the PTV.
source: In contrast and surprisingly, SSBs were almost as numerous at several centimeters from the limit of the beam as inside the PTV.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by the experimental data.

claim: SSBs are induced by photons propagating inside the material, confirming that the internal scattering is the major source of the dose deposited in the most proximal margin.
source: Moreover, we demonstrated that their formation necessitates continuity in the material from the PTV. This indicates that SSBs are induced by photons propagating inside the material, confirming several studies showing that the internal scattering is the major source of the dose deposited in the most proximal margin (Chofor et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by the experimental data and citations.

claim: The preferential generation of SSBs on DSBs in the margin could be the consequence of the tightening of the scattered photon spectral energy fluence distribution around lower energies.
source: Moreover, it can be hypothesized that the preferential generation of SSBs on DSBs in the margin could be the consequence of the tightening of the scattered photon spectral energy fluence distribution around lower energies (Chofor et al., 2012; Chofor et al., 2011; Kirkby et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: The ratio of DSBs/SSBs is very important in the cell outcome determination.
source: The results of this study also suggest that the ratio of DSBs/SSBs is very important in the cell outcome determination.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion drawn from the findings.

claim: Cells, whether they are cancerous or normal, developed both DSBs and SSBs when positioned inside the PTV, and consequently either underwent apoptosis in a few days, or more slowly entered a senescent-like state and then died.
source: Indeed, our data show that cells, whether they are cancerous or normal, developed both DSBs and SSBs when positioned inside the PTV, as already known (Reisz et al., 2014), and consequently either underwent apoptosis in a few days, or more slowly entered a senescent-like state and then died.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by the experimental data.

claim: Normal cells positioned at the margin, which developed almost exclusively SSBs, or normal cells in which almost exclusively SSBs were induced by a co-treatment with a mild concentration of H2O2 associated with a PARP inhibitor did not die at a significant level but entered senescence.
source: In contrast, normal cells positioned at the margin, which developed almost exclusively SSBs, or normal cells in which we induced almost exclusively SSBs by a co-treatment with a mild concentration of H2O2 associated with a PARP inhibitor did not die at a significant level but entered senescence.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by the experimental data.

claim: In all situations where senescence is induced by SSBs in the almost absence of DSBs, telomere shortening or any other DNA damage able to induce the DDR pathway, a few cells systematically re-enter in S-phase to generate a progeny of daughter cells displaying neoplastic or pre-neoplastic properties.
source: Very importantly, in all these situations where senescence is induced by SSBs in the almost absence of DSBs, telomere shortening or any other DNA damage able to induce the DDR pathway, a few cells systematically re-enter in S-phase to generate a progeny of daughter cells displaying neoplastic or pre-neoplastic properties (Deruy et al., 2010; Gosselin et al., 2009b; Martin et al., 2014; Nassour et al., 2016 and results herein).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations and the current study's data.

claim: NHDFs having entered in replicative senescence because of shortened telomeres never undergo apoptosis and remain very stably arrested in G1 without ever escaping.
source: In contrast, NHDFs (the same as those used in the irradiation experiments of this study), having entered in replicative senescence because of shortened telomeres, never undergo apoptosis and remain very stably arrested in G1 without ever escaping (d'Adda di Fagagna et al., 2003; Nassour et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Replicative senescence fits very well with the dogma equating senescence with tumor suppression.
source: This state of replicative senescence fits very well with the dogma equating senescence with tumor suppression (Campisi, 2005; Campisi, 2001; Kirkland and Tchkonia, 2017; Shay and Roninson, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: SSB-only-induced senescence, which harbors a cell cycle arrest that is not so stable for a few cells and source of cells harboring cancerous hallmarks, has to be considered as a tumor-promoting state.
source: In contrast, SSB-only-induced senescence, which harbors a cell cycle arrest that is not so stable for a few cells and source of cells harboring cancerous hallmarks, has to be considered as a tumor-promoting state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion drawn from the findings.

claim: Senescence establishment implies the accumulation of DNA breaks, some of which have to remain unrepaired to sustain a prolonged activation of the cell cycle arrest pathways.
source: Senescence establishment implies the accumulation of DNA breaks, some of which have to remain unrepaired to sustain a prolonged activation of the cell cycle arrest pathways.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and reflects established knowledge about senescence.

claim: In replicative senescence, shortened telomeres, which are assimilated to unrepaired DSBs, constantly activate the DDR pathway and downstream the tumor suppressor TP53 and its target p21.
source: This is true for replicative senescence in which shortened telomeres, which are assimilated to unrepaired DSBs, constantly activate the DDR pathway and downstream the tumor suppressor TP53 and its target p21, a CKI (Rossiello et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: In SSB-only-induced senescence of human keratinocytes and mammary epithelial cells, unrepaired SSBs activate the upregulation of p16.
source: This is also true for SSB-only-induced senescence of human keratinocytes and mammary epithelial cells where unrepaired SSBs activate the upregulation of p16 (Nassour et al., 2016), a major in vivo and in vitro senescence-associated CKI (He and Sharpless, 2017; Rayess et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: The precise mechanism of the PARylation capacity decline is presently unknown and is under investigation.
source: However, the precise mechanism of the PARylation capacity decline is presently unknown and is under investigation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a knowledge gap.

claim: The accumulation of unrepaired SSBs is the inducer of senescence, but paradoxically it is also the fuel for post-senescence evasion.
source: The accumulation of unrepaired SSBs is the inducer of senescence, but paradoxically it is also the fuel for post-senescence evasion (Nassour et al., 2016), probably because of the mutagenic potential of unrepaired DNA breaks.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: The precise mechanisms by which SSBs induce senescence and (pre)neoplastic evasion remain to be investigated.
source: However, the precise mechanisms by which SSBs induce senescence and (pre)neoplastic evasion remain to be investigated.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a knowledge gap.

claim: Eliminating senescent cells in mice delays or decreases the incidence of age-related disorders, including cancer.
source: It is now widely established that senescence contributes to multiple age-related dysfunctions and diseases, and eliminating senescent cells in mice delays or decreases the incidence of these disorders, including cancer (Baker et al., 2011; Wissler Gerdes et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: There are presently two major senolytics whose efficacy was demonstrated in vitro and in mouse models: (i) the BH3 mimetics ABT-737 and ABT-263 (navitoclax) and (ii) the association of dasatinib + quercetin.
source: There are presently two major senolytics whose efficacy was demonstrated in vitro and in mouse models, and which are subject to clinical trials (Chang et al., 2016; Pan et al., 2017): (i) the BH3 mimetics ABT-737 and ABT-263 (navitoclax) and (ii) the association of dasatinib + quercetin.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Navitoclax, dasatinib, and quercetin are or were used in anticancer treatments.
source: Interestingly, navitoclax, dasatinib, and quercetin are or were used in anticancer treatments, presupposing that their use after radiation therapy to prevent from a second cancer emergence should not hamper the efficacy of the radiotherapy, even they could act additionally or synergistically with the treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and reflects knowledge about these drugs.
